questions.question: 'Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment' as a Fundamental Right in the Indian Constitution is given in which Article of the Constitution ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Article 16__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 16

 
 
• ​In regard to** public employment, equality of opportunity** is discussed in Article 16 of our constitution.
 
• **Article 16.1:-**
 
 
• The term "state" refers to the **central or state government**, state legislature, parliament, and all authorities and organizations governed by the Government of India.
 
• Every citizen of the nation will have** equal opportunities** whenever the state attempts to offer employment at a position controlled by "The state." Similar to how opportunities are the same for everyone, **laws are the same** for everyone.
 
 
 
• **Article 16.2:-**
 
 
• The government cannot discriminate against its citizens based on **religion, caste, birth, gender**, or descent when **offering employment** in state offices. Furthermore, none of the candidates will be disqualified based on these five criteria.
 
• Equal employment opportunity is the goal of both articles, but the Indian constitution only allows for the extension of articles 16.1 and 16.2 to offices controlled by "The State."
 
• This indicates that the state alone is obligated to adhere to article 16, not private organizations or employment with the state on a contract basis.
 
 
 
• **Article 16.3:-**
 
 
• Any **employment or appointment **in an office controlled by the state can be made subject to a residence requirement set by the **parliament**. Nobody can stop this.
 
• India has **22 official languages**, so it seems legitimate. Additionally, there are numerous** occupations **in which workers must interact with locals on a daily basis.
 
 
 
• **Article 16.4:-**
 
 
• Any **backward class** of citizens can have their **reservation** granted by the state. who, in the opinion of the state, are not adequately represented in the services provided by the state.
 
• Simply put, reservations can be granted by the government when **recruiting employees** for offices under their control. However, reservations can only be granted to members of the** lower class** and** not to members of the upper class** and the backward class must not be represented in government positions, and the government must do so.
 
 
 
• **Article 16.5:-**
 
 
• This indicates that the state can provide for the appointment of a person of the** same religion** to religious institutions.
 
• The fact that India is home to a **large number of different religions** lends credence to this provision.
 
• Additionally, each religion is** extremely sensitive** to its own** tradition.**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 14:-**

 
 
• **​**According to Article 14 of the Indian Constitution, all citizens are **treated equally under the law,** and it is against the law to discriminate based on gender, caste, religion, place of birth, or post.
 
• It is also a first **fundamental right** that talks about equality and demands that laws be made that allow for equal treatment.
 
 
 
• **Article 17:-**
 
 
• **​**It is against the law to practice **untouchability** in any form. Any disability that is enforced as a result of untouchability is illegal and subject to legal sanctions.
 
• From the perspective of equality before the law, Article 17 is also a significant provision (Article 14). It ensures **human dignity and social justice**, two rights that have been denied to a large portion of Indian society for centuries.
 
 
 
• **Article 15:-**
 
 
• **​**Any citizen shall not be subjected to **discrimination** on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth, or any combination thereof.
 
• Access to shops, public restaurants, hotels, and places of public entertainment **shall not be restricted or denied** to any citizen solely on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth, or any combination thereof; or the utilization of wells, tanks, bathing ghats, roads, and places of the public resort that are either entirely or partially funded by the **state **and made available to the general public.

• A force **perpendicular** to the **magnetic field **and its own velocity acts on a **moving charge **in a magnetic field.
 
• **B** and **H** stand for the **magnetic field**. While the SI unit for B is Newtons per meter per ampere or **Teslas**, the SI unit for H is amperes per meter(A/m).

questions.question: Three resistors of 12 ohms, 16 ohms and 48 ohms are connected in parallel. What is the net resistance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 ohms.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Resistance**

 
 
• Electrical resistance, denoted by R, occurs when an **electric current passes through a conductor**, such as a light bulb. This** obstruction** is known as electrical resistance.
 
• Conductors generate** heat **when current passes through them because every material has **electrical resistance.**
 
• The following** factors** influence a conductor's electrical resistance:
 
 
• The **cross-sectional area** of the conductor
 
• **Length **of the conductor
 
• The** material** of the conductor
 
• The **temperature** of the conducting material
 
 
 
• The **series and parallel** configurations of resistors are the two most straightforward.
 
 
• **Resistors in Series:** When all of the resistors receive the **same amount of current**, they are said to be connected in series. The voltage across each resistor in such circuits varies. If any resistor **fails or a fault** occurs in a series connection, the entire circuit is **turned off.**
 
• **Resistors in Parallel**: When all of the resistors have the **same voltage**, they are considered to be connected in parallel. When these branches meet at a common point, the current is branched out and recombined in such circuits. In a parallel circuit, it is simple to connect or disconnect a resistor or any other component **without affecting** other components.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calculation**

 
 
• Three resistors given are,

 R₁= 12 ohm

 R₂= 16 ohm 

 R₃= 48 ohm 

 The formula for **total resistance **in parallel combination is** 1/Rₜₒₜ= 1/R₁+ 1/R₂+ 1/R₃**

 So, the total resistance

 1/Rₜₒₜ= 1/12+ 1/16+ 1/48

 1/Rₜₒₜ= 4+ 3+ 1/48

 1/Rₜₒₜ= 8/48

 1/Rₜₒₜ= 1/6

 **Rₜₒₜ= 6 ohms**

When a sphere is melted into 'n' equal smaller spheres, the new radius becomes r = R ÷ n¹/³.

Surface area of each new small ball = 4πr²

**∴ The correct answer is 314 2/7 cm².**

Radius of the original solid sphere (R) = 10 cm

**Calculations:**

Let the radius of each newly formed small spherical ball be r.

Since the large sphere is melted to form 8 identical balls, the total volume remains conserved.

⇒ Volume of large sphere = 8 × Volume of one small ball

⇒ 4/3 × π × R³ = 8 × (4/3 × π × r³)

⇒ R³ = 8 × r³

⇒ 10³ = 8 × r³

⇒ Surface Area = 314 2/7 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 314 2/7 cm².**

• Addition of hydrogen:

• Addition of electropositive element:
 
 
• SnCl₂ + 2HgCl₂ → SnCl₄ + Hg₂Cl₂ (**reduction of mercuric chloride**)
 
 
 
• Removal of oxygen
 
 
• ZnO + C → Zn + CO (**reduction of zinc oxide**)

questions.question: Nine years ago, P's age was twice the age of Q. If the ratio of their present ages is 5 ∶ 4, what is the sum of their present ages ?

**Given:**

Nine years ago, P's age was twice the age of Q

The ratio of their present ages is 5: 4

**Calculations:**

Let the present age of P is 5x

The present age of Q is 4x

Nine years ago,

⇒ The age of P = 5x - 9 

⇒ The age of Q = 4x - 9

According to the question,

⇒ (5x-9)/(4x-9)=(2)/(1)

⇒ 5x - 9 = 8x - 18

⇒ 8x - 5x = 18 - 9

⇒ 3x = 9

⇒ x = 3

⇒ Present age of P = 5x = 5 x 3 = 15 year

⇒ Present age of Q = 4x = 4 x 3 = 12 year

⇒ Sum of their age = 15 + 12 = 27 years

**⇒ Hence, The sum of the ages of P and Q is 27 years**

Identify the correct statement(s) with respect to the reflection of light by a spherical mirror from among the following.

• The spherical mirrors are painted on one side.
 
• Spherical mirrors are of two types:** Concave mirrors and convex mirrors.**
 
 
• In **concave mirrors**, the outward surface is painted and the inner surface is the reflecting surface.
 
• When the concave mirror is placed **close** to the object - a magnified, erect, and virtual image is formed.

questions.question: In macroeconomic analysis, marginal propensity to save (MPS) is _________.

options.text: the change in savings per unit change in income of an individual

__
 
• The **fraction** of increased **income** that is **saved **rather than **consumed** is known as the** marginal propensity to save** (MPS).
 
• MPS **fluctuates** **with income** and is generally greater at greater levels of income.
 
• MPS, a concept from **Keynesian macroeconomic theory**, is **computed by dividing** the change in income by the change in savings.
 
• The **Keynesian multiplier,** primarily explains the impact of additional funding or **government expenditure** as a **boost** to the economy, which is determined with the **aid of MPS**.
 
• The MPS of consumers can **help economic experts** predict how changes in government expenditure or **capital spending** would affect saving.
 
• A** savings line**, which has a slope due to the placement of change in savings on the** vertical y-axis** and change in income on the** horizontal x-axis**, is used to **represent MPS**.
 
• *Therefore, In macroeconomic analysis, marginal propensity to save (MPS) is the change in savings per unit change in income of an individual.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Keynes** was an outspoken **opponent of earlier economic views**, which he described as "mainstream economics," and he created his views in the aftermath of the **Great Depression.**
 
• The main **methods** advocated by Keynesian economics to steer the economy and combat poverty are **activist fiscal and financial policy**.

questions.question: The product of the LCM and the HCF of 18 and 25 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The product of the LCM and HCF of any two numbers is always equal to the product of the numbers themselves.

Required product = First number × Second number

Required product = 18 × 25 = 450

**∴ The correct answer is 450.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The given numbers are 18 and 25.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 25 = 5²

⇒ Since there are no common prime factors between the two numbers, their highest common factor will be 1.

⇒ HCF (18, 25) = 1

⇒ To find the LCM, we multiply the highest powers of all prime factors present.

⇒ LCM (18, 25) = 2 × 3² × 5²

⇒ LCM (18, 25) = 2 × 9 × 25 = 450

⇒ Product of LCM and HCF = 450 × 1

⇒ Product = 450

**∴ The correct answer is 450.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF Relationship

For any two natural numbers 'a' and 'b', the product of their LCM and HCF is exactly equal to the product of the two numbers themselves: LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b) = a × b. Note that this property applies strictly to pairs of numbers and not to three or more numbers.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers that have exactly 1 as their only common positive factor are known as co-prime or relatively prime numbers. For any pair of co-prime numbers, their HCF is always 1 and their LCM is always their direct product.

Fractions Rule

LCM of fractions = LCM of Numerators ÷ HCF of Denominators.
HCF of fractions = HCF of Numerators ÷ LCM of Denominators.

questions.question: What is covered under 'Maternal Health' ?

options.text: Care of all new mothers (after childbirth)
Care during prenatal, natal and post-natal period

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maternal health:-**

 
 
• It is referred to the health of women during pregnancy, childbirth, and the period after childbirth.
 
 
 
• **Prenatal period:**
 
 
• It is that time of pregnancy during which checkups from doctors, and nurses are taken throughout the pregnancy.
 
• Routine checkups and tests are done to ensure the proper development of the baby and mother.
 
• This phase is also called **pre-pregnancy care.**
 
 
 
• **Postpartum period:**
 
 
• This period starts after childbirth and its ending is marked by hormone levels and uterus size.
 
• This majorly ends in 6 weeks.
 
• But this is considered to be the most neglected phase in the lives of mothers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prenatal **checkups are typically scheduled as:

 
 
• Every 4 or 6 weeks for the first 32 weeks.
 
• Every 2 or 3 weeks for the 32 to 37 weeks.
 
• Every week from the 37th week until delivery.
 
 
 
• **Post-natal:**
 
 
• Most of the deaths occur during this period.
 
• This period has three phases:
 
 
• **Acute phase - **24 hours immediately after the delivery.
 
• **Sub-Acute phase -** can last up to 2-6 weeks after delivery.
 
• **Late Phase -** From 6 weeks - 6 months following delivery.​

questions.question: After the formation of the Janata Party government at Centre, which of the following multinationals shut its India operations due to compliance issue with the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act that mandated foreign investors cannot own over 40% in Indian enterprises?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• IBM and **Coca-Cola** stopped operating in **1977 **because they **couldn't adhere** to the **Foreign Exchange Regulation Act**, which prohibited international investors from owning more than** 40% **of Indian businesses.
 
• Following the 1977 elections, the **Janata Party** took office. In an effort to combat illegitimate wealth, **Prime Minister** **Morarji Desai** removed the legal tender validity from the 1,000, 5,000, and 10,000 rupee banknotes. Economic activity was impacted by Gandhi's ban on protests and the re-establishment of the union movement.

• Therefore, the correct answer is: *Coca-Cola*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Foreign Exchange Regulation Act**, also known as FERA, was first **presented in 1973**. The objective was to **retain India's** low foreign reserve status by regulating and controlling **foreign exchange**.
 
• This regulation **restricted** certain types of **payments**, supervised various foreign exchange operations, and **kept an eye on transactions** that affected **exchange rates**, imports, and export.
 
• FERA was passed with the intention of not just regulating and facilitating foreign exchange, but also of** increasing international trade** and payments and growing India's foreign **exchange reserves.**
 
• FERA violations are crimes that carry a direct prison sentence.
